VANTAGE — redesign handoff

A single-user moomoo portfolio tracker. Every screen below is the app as it stands today, drawn with the real tokens and the owner's real numbers, so a redesign starts from what exists rather than a description of it.

What the app is FOR: it tracks three US option-income ETFs held from Malaysia. The distributions are the strategy — price is down 11.8% while the holdings have paid out RM 5,033 net. Any redesign that treats this as a growth portfolio will tell the wrong story.

The three constraints that shape every screen: (1) two currencies, MYR and USD, that may never be summed without converting at the stored rate; (2) figures compared down a column are always tabular mono; (3) green is money in, red is money out — including tax and fees.

HOLDINGS — Positions (left) and Instruments (right)

Positions is the densest screen in the app and the one most in need of a rethink: eleven columns, three of them double-height. Instruments is the newest and least settled.

LEDGER — History (left) and Wallet (right)

364 history rows over nine months. The Wallet's headline balance comes from the broker while the list below it is an incomplete ledger — they deliberately disagree, and the screen has to make that legible.

PLANNING — Calendar (left) and Goals (right)

Goals carries five kinds across two shapes: accumulate shares, or reach an income level. Both answer 'how much more and what does it cost'.

SETTINGS

One real control — the P&L basis, which changes every P&L figure app-wide — plus read-only tax reporting. The three options preview the whole portfolio under each, so the choice is made by looking.

The manual-entry modals and the four states the shell resolves before any screen renders. Manual entry is the escape hatch for days the sync isn't running — it is not the main path, and shouldn't grow into one.
